correctness_confidence.basis: All main proofs in Sections 2-4 (torus-holonomy cancellation over C, Frobenius defect bound 8v, K_q mod-4 sign-counting obstruction, skew-Hadamard imaginary signing, and Clifford-cube recurrence including n=0) as well as the spectral values, characteristic polynomials, and switching-class counts in Table 1 were independently audited and verified without error.

novelty.basis: Establishes a clean universal no-go theorem over all of C for Cartesian products of two non-bipartite regular graphs, pairs it with a non-bipartite Clifford-cube lifting theorem to pinpoint the exact bipartiteness boundary, and frames conference vs. skew-Hadamard matrices as a sharp real-vs-complex Huang-signing dichotomy on K_q.

reproducibility.basis: All algebraic witnesses (Paley and doubling skew-Hadamard constructions, Clifford recurrence, explicit H(2,3) characteristic polynomials and Sturm brackets) are specified explicitly, and the two-layer verification scope separating the constructive Lean 4.36.0 arithmetic kernel from exact integer/rational Python certificates is transparently documented.

rigor.basis: Arguments are concise, exact, and free of floating-point approximations; the authors explicitly note which parts are formalized in Lean 4 (20 arithmetic/modular/moment/Sturm theorems) versus proved in the manuscript text (matrix plaquette cancellation, Hermitian interlacing, conference sign counting).

significance.basis: Clarifies the exact algebraic and topological limits of extending Huang-optimal signings to general regular graphs and Cartesian products, and separates operator-norm minimization from median Cauchy-interlacing eigenvalue maximization on concrete obstructed graphs such as H(2,3), K_5, and the Petersen graph.

summary: This manuscript establishes sharp algebraic and spectral boundaries for extending Huang-optimal signings (S^2 = dI) over both R and C to regular graphs and their Cartesian products. First, Theorem 1 proves that no Hermitian unit-modulus signing over C can achieve S^2 = (d_G + d_H)I on G box H when both factors are non-bipartite, because any odd-by-odd discrete torus forces the product of elementary 4-cycle holonomies to be simultaneously +1 (by edge-conjugate cancellation) and -1; it further derives a quantitative Frobenius defect ||S^2 - dI||_F^2 >= 8v for real signings and resolves all 1,024 real switching classes of H(2,3) = K_3 box K_3. Second, Theorem 2 contrasts real +/-1 signings on K_q (equivalent to symmetric conference matrices, forcing q = 2 mod 4) with purely imaginary {+/-i} signings derived from skew-Hadamard matrices (solving H_q^2 = (q-1)I_q for skew-Hadamard orders q = 0 mod 4), and proves that the block-Clifford recurrence lifts any real or complex Huang-optimal seed G_0 (even non-bipartite) to G_0 box Q_n. Third, Theorem 3 provides an exhaustive zero-float switching-class atlas across 11 canonical regular graphs, separating 4 real Huang-optimal graphs (including the non-bipartite octahedron J(4,2)) from 7 obstructed graphs.
strengths: Theorem 1(a) gives a remarkably clean, general topological-algebraic obstruction showing that arbitrary U(1) complex phases cannot bypass odd-by-odd discrete torus holonomy in G box H.

Theorem 1(c) and Table 1 cleanly demonstrate the divergence between minimizing ||S||_op and maximizing the Cauchy-interlacing median eigenvalue lambda_{ceil(n/2)}(S), exemplified on H(2,3) where min ||S||_op = (1+sqrt(17))/2 yet max lambda_5 = 1 < 2 while skewed -A achieves lambda_4 = 2 at ||S||_op = 4.
Theorem 2(b) proves that Clifford-cube lifting G_0 box Q_n requires neither bipartiteness of G_0 nor real entries, sharply complementing Theorem 1 at the bipartiteness boundary.
Transparent, honest delineation in Section 5 between the axiom-free Lean 4.36.0 arithmetic/Sturm/moment kernel and the matrix-level proofs and zero-float Python enumerations.
weaknesses: In Theorem 1(b), each elementary 4-cycle with W = +1 actually yields two unordered opposite-vertex pairs (four off-diagonal entries of magnitude 2), so the Frobenius defect bound could be tightened from 8v to 16v; the stated >= 8v bound remains valid but is slightly conservative.

In Theorem 2(a), the Paley skew-conference orthogonality for general primes p = 3 (mod 4) relies on classical citations [8, 10] rather than an inline proof, and general (non-purely-imaginary) U(1) Hermitian signings remain uncharacterized for non-conference orders such as q = 22.

Formal verification in Lean 4.36.0 covers the 20 scalar, parity, modular, moment, and Sturm-isolation theorems rather than full matrix-level linear algebra (plaquette cancellation and Hermitian Cauchy interlacing are proved on paper, and exhaustive graph enumerations rely on Layer 2 Python certificates).
Minor bibliographic typo in Reference [6] ('Hermitian adjacency matriz').
strong_novelty_candidates: Universal complex torus-holonomy no-go theorem on Cartesian products of two non-bipartite regular graphs over all of U(1) subset C (Theorem 1a).
Non-bipartite Clifford-cube lifting theorem (Theorem 2b) pinpointing the exact bipartite-vs-non-bipartite boundary for Cartesian products together with Theorem 1.
Complex-vs-real Huang-signing dichotomy on K_q linking symmetric conference matrices (q = 2 mod 4) and purely imaginary skew-Hadamard signings (q = 0 mod 4) (Theorem 2a).

Exhaustive zero-float 11-graph switching-class spectral atlas demonstrating exact factor-2 and 1/sqrt(3) median-eigenvalue collapses and real Huang-optimality of non-bipartite J(4,2) (Theorem 3, Table 1).
